fix_summary: clang-frep-pragma (d8864767cd03). (1) Attr.td Frep: let HasCustomParsing = 1, like LoopHint, so Sema accepts the 2 identifier args (pragma name, option) the parser passes, instead of "'frep' attribute takes one argument". (2) ParsePragma.cpp PragmaFrepHandler: the printf error paths become existing warnings (no new .td entry): '#pragma frep' / '#pragma frep(infer)' -> warn_pragma_expected_identifier; '#pragma frep bogus' -> warn_pragma_invalid_argument "...; expected 'infer'"; '#pragma frep infer extra' -> warn_pragma_extra_tokens_at_eol, now checked before the value tokens are collected (before, this check was dead code and the pragma was kept with a printf 'Not EOF'). All in -Wignored-pragmas (default on); each ignores the pragma, like #pragma unroll / #pragma riscv. The unreachable printf branches in HandlePragmaFrep, ParsePragmaFrep and handleFrepAttr become asserts that the option is 'infer'. (3) CGStmt.cpp EmitStmt: emit llvm.riscv.frep.infer only when getTarget().hasFeature("xfrep"); without Xfrep it was a backend fatal error 'Cannot select: intrinsic %llvm.riscv.frep.infer' on GAP9/rv32imafd. Also scan the whole attribute list, not only Attrs[0]: '#pragma unroll 1' before '#pragma frep infer' silently dropped the marker. passes (92bb3ac8cc98): SNITCHFrepLoops.cpp also drops leftover PseudoFrepInfer when skipFunction() is true (-O0, optnone). Before, the asm printer asserted 'Cannot print this instruction'. The existing sweep is now a helper, removeFrepInferPseudos.
consumer: The marker is not metadata. CodeGen emits 'call void @llvm.riscv.frep.infer()' before the loop. RISCVInstrInfoXfrep.td:52 selects it to PseudoFrepInfer (HasExtXfrep). SNITCHFrepLoops::isMarkedForInference looks for it in the MachineLoop preheader and runs inference for that loop even without -snitch-frep-inference. The old 'frep' metadata code in addFrepMetadata was already commented out in the fork.
rule8: Pre-existing fork defect, not an LLVM 20 regression. Fork origin: f1b7aebff8c2 '[LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms' (pulp/integer_SIMD_fix; the Frep attr, parser, CGStmt and pass pseudo sweep all come from it). The Sema rejection comes from upstream fa4e72971e05 'Automate common diagnostic checking for statement attributes' (llvmorg-13): statement attributes get the generic argument-count check unless HasCustomParsing is set. Reference: LoopHint 'let HasCustomParsing = 1' clang/include/clang/Basic/Attr.td:4346 and ParsePragmaLoopHint clang/lib/Parse/ParseStmt.cpp:2537 at llvmorg-20.1.8. Diagnostics follow PragmaRISCVHandler (ParsePragma.cpp:4162, warn_pragma_invalid_argument) and PragmaUnrollHintHandler (ParsePragma.cpp:3760, warn_pragma_extra_tokens_at_eol) at llvmorg-20.1.8.

other_errors_seen: NEW, serious, pre-existing (ref-18 and int-20 with -snitch-frep-inference produce identical output): SNITCHFrepLoops miscompiles a loop-carried FP accumulator. For 'acc += ssr_pop(0)*ssr_pop(1)' x128 it emits 'fcvt.d.w fa5,zero; li a0,127; frep.o a0,1,0,0; fmadd.d fa0,ft0,ft1,fa5; fmv.x.w a0,fa5'. Each iteration reads the initial 0 (fa5) instead of fa0, so the result is the last product only, and a stray fmv.x.w follows. The pragma only makes this reachable from source. llvm/test/CodeGen/RISCV/freploop.ll hwloop2 checks only 'fmadd.d {{.*}}', so it cannot catch this. Probably SNITCHFrepLoops::fixupPHIs; needs a backlog row (passes cluster).

SNITCHFrepLoops does not infer loops with a runtime trip count behind a zero-trip guard (for i<n): 'trip count not found' for the count-down form (ADDI -1 compared with x0). Same with the global flag. Separately, the '#pragma frep infer' marker lands in the entry block, while the MachineLoop preheader is a split 'for.body.preheader', so isMarkedForInference would not find it either. Pass limitation (passes cluster).

handleFrepAttr accepts only ForStmt, but reuses err_pragma_loop_precedes_nonloop, which says 'expected a for, while, or do-while loop to follow #pragma frep'. So a while loop is rejected with a message claiming while loops are accepted. Pre-existing, clang-frep-pragma.
Without Xfrep, '#pragma frep infer' is dropped silently (no diagnostic); a warning would need a new diagnostic or a reuse decision.
FrepAttr::printPrettyPragma prints nothing, so -ast-print loses the pragma. Pre-existing, cosmetic.
